results.title: RISs as Enablers for Adaptive and Modular Space Communication Architectures
results.abstract: The increasing demand for agile, energy-efficient, and software-defined space communication systems has brought intelligent electromagnetic surfaces into the spotlight as key enabling technologies. This paper explores the role of reconfigurable and intelligent metasurfaces in shaping next-generation space architectures. By passively manipulating wavefronts through programmable sub-wavelength elements, metasurfaces can enhance link quality, provide dynamic coverage steering, and reduce onboard processing and energy demands-particularly beneficial in small satellite and distributed Low-Earth Orbit (LEO) constellations. We discuss architectural scenarios where metasurfaces support modular and adaptive connectivity in space-to-space and space-to-ground systems. Furthermore, we explore how metasurfaces, when controlled via Artificial Intelligence (AI) or embedded logic, contribute to the vision of interoperable, software-defined, and updateable space infrastructures. The paper concludes with a roadmap for integrating intelligent metasurfaces into space digital twins, onboard optimization loops, and standardized interfaces for future cognitive space systems. © 2026 IEEE.

results.title: Integrated Attitude Control Architecture for Manipulator-Equipped SmallSats
results.abstract: As interest in on-orbit servicing, assembly, and debris removal grows, small satellite platforms must be adapted for contactbased operations using robotic manipulators. These missions introduce strong dynamic coupling between the manipulator and the bus, often with comparable mass and inertia, which challenges conventional Attitude Determination and Control Systems (ADCS). This work presents an ADCS architecture and control algorithm tailored to small satellites equipped with manipulators. A digital twin integrates a multibody dynamics model of the satellite-manipulator system with a full ADCS suite (reaction wheels, star tracker, gyroscope, accelerometer) and a quaternion-based PD controller. To mitigate internal disturbances induced by manipulator, a feedforward control layer anticipates and compensates reaction forces and torques at the manipulator base. The approach is demonstrated during the comissioning phase of the manipulator post de-tumble. Preliminary results indicate that manipulator disturbances can dominate environmental torques, necessitating dedicated compensation. The feedforward controller method improves pointing during slow manipulator motions at the cost of higher actuator workload; controller gains must adapt in real time to manipulator pose. By iterating within the digital twin, the ADCS design is optimized with manipulator behavior and operations, enabling robust, cost-effective control for small-satellite missions with complex dynamics. The use of the digital twin can extend the use of low-cost platforms into domains traditionally reserved for larger spacecraft while preserving systemlevel performance and reliability. © 2026 IEEE.

results.title: Depth and Geometry Regularization for Neural Implicit Reconstruction from Few-View Satellite Images
results.abstract: High-precision 3-D reconstruction from a small number of optical satellite images is crucial for applications such as disaster response, urban monitoring, and digital twins. However, under few-view conditions, both traditional multiview stereo (MVS) pipelines and recent neural radiance field (NeRF)-based reconstruction methods suffer from weak geometric observability and significant illumination variations, which often lead to unstable geometry and characteristic failure modes, such as shadow-induced artifacts and height drift. To address these challenges, we propose DGR-NeRF, a neural implicit surface reconstruction method with depth and geometric regularization designed for few-view satellite imagery. The proposed method represents scene geometry using a signed distance function (SDF) and introduces complementary geometric constraints to stabilize the ill-posed geometry-radiance optimization. Specifically, relative structural information from monocular depth estimation is incorporated to guide geometric ordering and reduce shadow-related ambiguities, while sparse SfM points (SSPs) are used as soft geometric anchors to improve global spatial consistency and elevation accuracy. In addition, we design a geometric validity regularization (GVR) that enforces physically plausible SDF behavior, suppressing nonphysical artifacts such as inverted pseudosurfaces and abnormal holes during training. Experiments on DFC2019 and IARPA2016 datasets demonstrate that DGR-NeRF can generate meshes and digital surface models (DSMs) with complete structures and high geometric accuracy using as few as five input satellite images, significantly outperforming existing reconstruction methods under few-view conditions. Code is available at https://github.com/Ljy0109/DGR-NeRF. © 1980-2012 IEEE.

results.title: Quantum Machine Learning for Wireless-Powered UAV Positioning in 6G Digital Twin SAGIN with Cooperative Nano-Satellite Constellations
results.abstract: Energy-efficient space-air-ground integrated networks (SAGINs) are vital for sustainable communications. This study presents an energy-aware SAGIN framework that utilizes a uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV)-mounted mobile edge computing (MEC) platform enhanced by digital-twin technology, UAV energy harvesting via wireless power transfer, and a nano-satellite constellation with MEC facilities. We formulate a joint optimization problem for UAV trajectory planning, task offloading, computational resource allocation, and satellite load balancing as a mixed-integer nonlinear programming (MINLP) problem that minimizes the weighted system cost while satisfying energy and latency constraints. To address this complex problem, two quantum-driven deep reinforcement learning (QD-DRL) algorithms namely quantum-driven cost-effective advantage actor-critic (QD-CE-A2C) and quantum-driven cost-effective proximal policy optimization (QD-CE-PPO) are proposed. These algorithms employ angle encoding with learnable parameters and variational quantum neural networks to enhance policy exploration and accelerate convergence. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed QD-DRL approaches achieve superior cost efficiency and ensure effective service to all access points within the defined mission duration. Moreover, QD-DRL approaches achieved higher cumulative rewards and faster convergence compared to classical DRL baselines. Consequently, the proposed frameworks provide a scalable and intelligent paradigm for cost-efficient resource management in future 6G-enabled SAGINs. © 1983-2012 IEEE.

results.title: Evaluating Metamodel Quality of the Cubesat System Reference Model (CSRM) to Improve Domain-Specific Languages (DSL)
results.abstract: This paper investigates the CubeSat System Reference Model (CSRM) to objectively evaluate quality metrics Incorporating the CSRM into systems engineering (SE) processes can strengthen communication and collaboration across the enterprise. Providing domain-specific additions to the Systems Modeling Language (SysML), the CSRM profile establishes specialized model elements meant to facilitate mission architectures for CubeSats using a model-based systems engineering (MBSE) approach. Its development is an ongoing effort led by the International Council of Systems Engineering (INCOSE) Space Systems Working Group (SSWG), with a beta specification published by the Object Management Group (OMG). The working group aims to standardize the CubeSat system design across the industry and improve transparency in product development. Domain analysis realizes that external groups affected by CubeSats include governments, regulatory organizations, space agencies, research institutions, aerospace manufacturers, launch services providers, and various end users. With such a wide variety of invested individuals, eliciting quality requirements directly has proven to be an arduous task. Instead, the Quality Model for Metamodels (QM4MM) framework and associated metrics will be used to define verifiable requirements. Evaluating these metrics will provide CSRM contributors with guidance to address weaknesses in robustness and improve the specification. By leveraging the metamodel to quantify measurements, this study supports the next iteration of the CSRM and mitigates potential quality concerns. This research is anticipated to complement best practices for the greater technical community when creating new domain-specific languages (DSL) in MBSE environments. © 2026 IEEE.

results.title: RISs as Enablers for Adaptive and Modular Space Communication Architectures
results.abstract: The increasing demand for agile, energy-efficient, and software-defined space communication systems has brought intelligent electromagnetic surfaces into the spotlight as key enabling technologies. This paper explores the role of reconfigurable and intelligent metasurfaces in shaping next-generation space architectures. By passively manipulating wavefronts through programmable sub-wavelength elements, metasurfaces can enhance link quality, provide dynamic coverage steering, and reduce onboard processing and energy demands-particularly beneficial in small satellite and distributed Low-Earth Orbit (LEO) constellations. We discuss architectural scenarios where metasurfaces support modular and adaptive connectivity in space-to-space and space-to-ground systems. Furthermore, we explore how metasurfaces, when controlled via Artificial Intelligence (AI) or embedded logic, contribute to the vision of interoperable, software-defined, and updateable space infrastructures. The paper concludes with a roadmap for integrating intelligent metasurfaces into space digital twins, onboard optimization loops, and standardized interfaces for future cognitive space systems.

results.title: Integrated Attitude Control Architecture for Manipulator-Equipped SmallSats
results.abstract: As interest in on-orbit servicing, assembly, and debris removal grows, small satellite platforms must be adapted for contactbased operations using robotic manipulators. These missions introduce strong dynamic coupling between the manipulator and the bus, often with comparable mass and inertia, which challenges conventional Attitude Determination and Control Systems (ADCS). This work presents an ADCS architecture and control algorithm tailored to small satellites equipped with manipulators. A digital twin integrates a multibody dynamics model of the satellite-manipulator system with a full ADCS suite (reaction wheels, star tracker, gyroscope, accelerometer) and a quaternion-based PD controller. To mitigate internal disturbances induced by manipulator, a feedforward control layer anticipates and compensates reaction forces and torques at the manipulator base. The approach is demonstrated during the comissioning phase of the manipulator post de-tumble. Preliminary results indicate that manipulator disturbances can dominate environmental torques, necessitating dedicated compensation. The feedforward controller method improves pointing during slow manipulator motions at the cost of higher actuator workload; controller gains must adapt in real time to manipulator pose. By iterating within the digital twin, the ADCS design is optimized with manipulator behavior and operations, enabling robust, cost-effective control for small-satellite missions with complex dynamics. The use of the digital twin can extend the use of low-cost platforms into domains traditionally reserved for larger spacecraft while preserving systemlevel performance and reliability.

results.title: AI-Driven Digital Engineering Platform for Rapid CubeSat Mission Prototyping
results.abstract: The growing adoption of nanosatellites has significantly expanded access to space-based experimentation and education. However, early-stage CubeSat design and mission conceptualization remain challenging for students and first-time developers because of fragmented tools and steep learning curves. This paper presents NanoSatPlay, an AI-enabled, browser-based platform that unifies CubeSat design, configuration, orbit visualization, and intelligent design guidance within a single interactive environment. The system integrates a visual component-based satellite designer, a real-time three-dimensional orbit simulator, and a generative AI assistant that provides subsystem-level feedback and contextual learning support. By lowering technical barriers and emphasizing visual and experiential learning, NanoSatPlay enables rapid prototyping, systems-level understanding, and effective STEM education. The architecture, core features, and educational benefits of the platform are discussed, demonstrating its potential to democratize nanosatellite engineering.

results.title: A Steam Engine for the Space Age: Thermodynamic Analysis of a Detonation Thruster withWater Electrolysis Propellant Generation
results.abstract: A thermodynamic model of a water electrolysis system is developed and integrated into a thermodynamic system model of a detonative combustion engine to enable the analysis of theoretical small-spacecraft detonation propulsion systems usingwater electrolysis for propellant generation. Due to the additional time required to generate propellants via electrolysis, these thrusters lend themselves well to infrequent, impulsive firings rather than sustained burns. Performance characteristics including specific impulse, energy efficiency, and a theoretical maximum impulse are identified for a representative nanosatellite-class spacecraft thruster with ideal and nonideal detonation combustion operation using an annular combustor with a plug nozzle and compared to deflagration operation using a traditional converging-diverging nozzle. The volume savings from stored liquid water propellant are also quantified compared to compressed gas tanks with equivalent thruster performance, with some configurations representing a volume reduction of multiple orders of magnitude. Results suggest that the in-space detonation thruster architectures characterized in this analysis are potentially attractive for applications such as station-keeping or orbital transfers. © 2026, American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics Inc, AIAA. results.title: Space qualification of AWG-based FBG interrogators: the road toward CubeSat implementation [Invited]
results.abstract: Photonic integrated circuits (PICs) offer a pathway to miniaturized fiber Bragg grating (FBG) interrogators for structural health monitoring aboard satellites. However, the environmental resilience of PIC-based components remains insufficiently investigated compared to their discrete counterparts. This study reports the environmental testing of a silicon oxynitride arrayed waveguide grating (AWG) as a key component of an FBG interrogator, and presents an interrogator layout designed for the CubeSat form-factor. Vibration testing under Soyuz-2 launch profiles for secondary payloads confirmed the structural integrity of the AWG, with no performance degradation observed. Thermal vacuum cycling of AWG (−20°C to +80°C) revealed a linear spectral shift of (+11 ± 1) pm/°C across its channels, which is algorithmically compensable. γ-irradiation with a total ionizing dose of 2.8 krd induced a mean spectral shift of 63 pm in the AWG channels, indicating the necessity for radiation hardening measures. The presented study demonstrates the viability of AWG-based FBG interrogators for space applications. © 2026 Chinese Optics Letters.

results.title: A Concurrent Model-Based Systems Engineering Methodology for SmallSat Lunar Mission Design
results.abstract: This paper presents a Concurrent Model-Based Systems Engineering (CE–MBSE) methodology aimed at improving the design of complex space missions by combining the collaborative nature of Concurrent Engineering (CE) with the rigor and traceability of Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE). The proposed approach is centred on an integrated system model acting as a single source of truth across all lifecycle phases, enabling consistent management of requirements, system architectures, and multidisciplinary data. The methodology adapts concurrent workflows to different maturity stages, from early mission definition to verification and operational phases, while progressively increasing model fidelity. A modular and interoperable toolchain is introduced, integrating the Capella MBSE environment with the Altium Requirements & System Portal (RSP) through Python-based synchronization mechanisms, ensuring digital continuity and real-time data consistency across domains. The approach is validated through its application to the BioMoon mission, a lunar CubeSat constellation designed to investigate the radiation environment and its effects on biological systems. Results demonstrate improved traceability across abstraction levels, enhanced multidisciplinary coordination, and the effective integration of simulation-driven verification within the design loop, while highlighting some challenges related to toolchain complexity, synchronisation overhead, and scalability to larger and more complex systems. Overall, the CE–MBSE methodology represents a promising framework to support coherent, knowledge-driven, and lifecycle-oriented design processes for next-generation space missions. © 2026, The Authors. results.title: Design and Virtual-Twin Validation of an Energy-Aware S-Band Communication Subsystem for a 6U CubeSat (30 × 20 × 10 cm)
results.abstract: This study outlines a practical design for an energy-conscious S-band communication system meant for a 6U CubeSat measuring 30 by 20 by 10 centimeters. Instead of building only physical prototypes, the approach uses a digital twin method to test designs early. That way, key decisions get checked well before finalizing any actual hardware. The full setup covers everything from radio frequency components to data framing aligned with CCSDS standards. Error protection during transmission is included too. Processing happens through flexible electronics - software-driven logic on FPGA chips handles the signal tasks A chip plus two antennas set up for stable signal during spin. Testing three ways to send data: one basic radio path, another smarter S-band method adjusting speed using phase shifts while switching between patches, also a bigger unfolding dish idea for more volume. With clear rules like orbit height at 500 km, Earth station size near 1.2 meters, losses guessed on the safe side, it calculates how much power each connection needs, checks flow rates when satellites rise above horizon, probes error risks tied to different wave patterns used. Findings tilt toward smart QPSK with flexible code strength paired with twin surface antennas - handles dropouts well, saves battery life per useful chunk sent, stays manageable to build, fits tight spaces too. Mirror-world technique ties math models of signals, satellite paths overhead, juice supply timing, heat limits from active periods into a cycle that runs again and again, testing contact success ahead of flight under varied operational scenes. The proposed architecture demonstrates a practical and energy-efficient communication framework suitable for 6U CubeSat missions under constrained orbital and power conditions. - a way to piece together small systems reliably. Testing fits within tight constraints typical of tiny satellites. Results can be checked again by others. This method holds up even when tools and time are scarce. © 2026, CC BY.

results.title: A Comparative Review and Methodological Framework for CubeSat Telemetry Downlink Architecture
results.abstract: The telemetry downlink subsystem plays a key role in maintaining reliable communication between CubeSats and their ground station. However, CubeSats operate under stringent constraints in power, bandwidth and processing capability, which often necessitate trade-offs in selecting modulation and coding schemes. This paper reviews telemetry downlink architectures implemented in recent CubeSat missions, examining each system in terms of modulation strategy, transmitter power, data rate, operating frequency, antenna configuration and mission type. The review shows that most CubeSat telemetry downlinks rely on static UHF configurations. While this approach supports reliability and implementation simplicity, it offers limited adaptability to the dynamic link conditions experienced during an orbital pass, potentially leading to underutilised link margin and reduced efficiency. More flexible downlink architectures are observed in some missions, but these are typically associated with payload data transmission or require system resources that exceed typical CubeSat constraints. In response to these observations, this paper proposes a telemetry downlink framework based on Variable Coded Modulation (VCM). The framework introduced adaptive MODCOD selection to better utilise link margin under time-varying channel conditions while maintaining reliability. It serves as a reference model for future validation and practical implementation in CubeSat telemetry systems. © 2026, The Aeronautical and Astronautical Society of the Republic of China. results.title: Mixed Dark Matter: Limits from the Milky Way Satellite Galaxies
results.abstract: The Standard Model of particle physics contains a diverse set of particle species, motivating the possibility of a similarly complex dark sector. Here we study two-component dark matter (DM) mixtures, in which one component behaves as standard CDM while the other suppresses the formation of small-scale structure, either through an astrophysically relevant de Broglie wavelength (fuzzy DM; FDM) or collisional damping from temperature-independent scattering (interacting DM; IDM). Using the observed population of Milky Way satellite galaxies, we derive new leading constraints on the parameter spaces of mixed FDM and of mixed IDM coupled to photons (γ-DM), neutrinos (ν-DM), or baryons (p-DM), for beyond-CDM fractions down to 50%. We require that the linear matter power spectra of allowed models remain less suppressed than a constrained reference model. The resulting 95% confidence bounds on FDM mass and IDM cross section weaken systematically with decreasing fraction, following distinct power-law scalings. At 50% fraction, IDM cross section bounds weaken by a factor of ∼2–6 and FDM mass bounds by ∼1.5, relative to the 100% case. We forecast that idealized future satellite surveys, which adopt approximate LSST sensitivity thresholds, can improve these 100% bounds by a factor of ∼1.6–14 for IDM and ∼3 for FDM. Self-consistent cosmological simulations of mixed DM scenarios will be essential to more robustly characterize the degeneracy between particle physics parameters and fractional contribution, to extend constraints to lower fractions, and to identify signatures beyond satellite abundance to further inform these models. results.title: Impact of Future 5G Deployments on X-Band Earth Observation Downlinks
results.abstract: The 8.025–8.400 GHz band is one of the key X-band downlink ranges for modern Earth observation satellites, enabling high-rate transmission of imagery and sensor data for agriculture, environmental monitoring, greenhouse gas assessment, disaster response and security-related applications. The potential introduction of 5G networks into this band raises serious concerns about harmful interference to Earth observation ground stations cand, consequently, about the continuity and growth of the global Earth observation data chain. This paper investigates the feasibility of sharing this downlink band between Earth observation systems and 5G networks using a Monte Carlo simulation framework. The model includes a low-Earth-orbit Earth observation satellite with dynamically tracking ground stations and dense urban, suburban and rural deployments of 5G base stations and user devices, together with established radio-propagation and clutter models and representative protection objectives for satellite downlinks. The results suggest that, to keep interference at acceptable levels, ground stations would need to be located far from 5G deployments, which is difficult to achieve in practice and could seriously limit the future expansion of Earth observation infrastructure. © 2026 by the authors.

results.title: Digital Twin Simulation and Verification System Design and Implementation for Satellite Production Lines
results.abstract: In this paper, we focus on satellite production lines and design and implement a digital twin simulation and verification system for them. This is to improve manual documentation efficiency and provide sufficient process controllability in the small satellites' batch production and assembly testing. We built a layered architecture. This allows the system to dynamically interact with AIT data management systems, structured process systems, and equipment data by fusing multi-source data. We also develop functional modules that combine lightweight 3D model visualization, dynamic simulation engines, and hybrid scheduling optimization algorithms. These modules can perform twin simulation, execute processes, intelligently schedule production, manage work reporting, conduct intelligent analysis, trigger anomaly alarms, and perform system management. We also dynamically simulate complex workflows like satellite transfer and automated assembly. These workflows are then verified using 3D virtual scene modeling and physical engines. We use time-series analysis to improve scheduling accuracy and multidimensional dynamic monitoring and hierarchical response to enhance production stability. In practice, the system can provide visualized control over the full process of satellite production. This greatly improves assembly efficiency and process controllability. It can also be an extensible digital way for aerospace manufacturing. The use of hierarchical architecture design and multimodal data fusion can be further applied in the complex equipment intelligent manufacturing. © 2026 SAE International.

results.title: Thermal control with digital twins for dimensional stability in CubeSat payloads
results.abstract: Small satellites are on the rise within the context of the so-called New Space industry, driven by the use of cost-efficient, off-the-shelf components as well as miniaturization, modularity, and scalability. While this opens many opportunities, especially in terms of accessibility to space, it also comes with its challenges. When high-precision optical sensors are employed, such as laser-based communication systems, payload temperature gradients often lead to optical aberrations due to the satellite’s uneven thermal expansion. This reduces reliability and hinders the system’s performance in certain stages of the mission. Moreover, traditional methods to alleviate temperature gradients, such as heat pipes, might be infeasible due to limited payload volume, and control routines might fail due to structural degradation and component wear. This paper presents an innovative approach to achieving thermal stability in a Dynamic Optical Ranging & Timing system by exploiting the waste heat of redundant electronic components. An Onboard Digital Twin is defined, composed of a satellite thermal model, model-predictive control to schedule the load of redundant electronic components, and a parameter updating scheme that accounts for time-variant internal and external deviations. The framework was executed off-board in a laboratory hardware-testing environment, with the measured control timings supporting the computational feasibility of future deployment on the target multi-processor onboard computer. During the hardware tests, the presented framework achieved a maximum relative temperature error of under 10 % between model prediction and measurement data, and successfully maintained temperature differences between critical components below the required 5 K. © 2026 The Authors.
